who_can_apply: Girls ages 7 to 18 for workshops. A separate College and Careers Community serves ages 18 plus.
how_to_apply: Check the community events page for current workshops: community.wearebgc.org/events.
notes: The home page did not name a Bay Area chapter, prices or workshop dates. Check the events page for what is open now. Code Along videos are free on YouTube. Home page shows no workshop price, so the card is not in the paid group.
pay_detail: Workshop cost and pay are not stated on the home page. The Code Along videos on YouTube are free. The page does not say anyone is paid.

who_can_apply: People 14 and older (the page also welcomes adults). Parents of kids under 14 can email musicsp@iu.edu. You do not need an audition or past experience.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form and pay the deposit and tuition. Questions go to musicsp@iu.edu.
notes: There is also a summer intensive linked from the page. Group class is Tuesdays 8:30 to 9:30 p.m. Eastern.
pay_detail: Track 1 (private lessons plus group class) $800. Track 2 (group class only) $550. A $50 non-refundable deposit is credited to tuition.

who_can_apply: High school students with a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale. The page says the experience is open to all students. Selective, seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Online application: 100-word statement, 250-word response, GPA and business-related activities. No exceptions for missed deadlines.
notes: The page lists weekday dates (for example 'Wednesday April 7') that match 2027, and a fall 2026 virtual session (Oct 13 and 20, 2026) whose application closed Sept 25, 2026. Applications are not reviewed until after the deadline.
duration: One day in person, or two virtual sessions
pay_detail: No registration fees; breakfast and lunch provided. In-person students pay their own travel to Bloomington, housing and personal costs.

who_can_apply: High school students who care about the environment. The program is online.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the 2027 application opens in January 2027. Questions: essi@iu.edu.
notes: Entirely online, so students anywhere can join. The page shows quotes from 9th, 10th and 11th grade alumni. Participants receive a certificate of completion.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students who live or attend high school in the United States and finish the online course and the separate summer application. You must be in the US for the July program. The page lists no age or citizenship rule.
how_to_apply: Sign yourself up through the self-register link on the Summer Program Application page (mit-bwsi.formstack.com). No nomination is needed. Or have a teacher or mentor nominate you. Later you need three essays of 500 words or less each. You need a teacher or mentor recommendation. You need parent or guardian information with an electronic signature. You also need to finish the online prerequisite course. Contact: bwsi-admin@mit.edu.
notes: Competitive. The cost wording on the page leaves the $200,000 to $200,001 range unclear, so ask BWSI if you are near that line. The online course is free and stays open to independent learners.
duration: Four week program in July. The online prerequisite course opens February 1.
pay_detail: Families with income and assets under $200,000 pay nothing. Families above that pay $3,000 (housing is not covered for in person programs). No stipend is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Middle or high school students who are US residents at the time of submission (citizenship not required). Students may compete in the district where they live or where they attend school. Solo or teams up to four. At least half the team must be eligible for the district the team competes in.
how_to_apply: Register on the Student Registration page, then submit the app online.
notes: Any language or platform is allowed, solo or teams up to four. Check the Participating Districts page on the site to confirm your district takes part.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students at schools with a DECA chapter. A school without one can request a new chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask the DECA advisor at your high school. If there is no chapter, use the Start a Chapter link on the page or contact info@deca.org or (703) 860-5000.
notes: State groups run the local contests. This guide already lists California, Georgia and Illinois DECA. Dues, travel and conference costs were not on the page, so ask your advisor.
pay_detail: Membership cost is not listed on the page. Ask your chapter advisor.

who_can_apply: The site lists Posts for ages 14 to 20 (and Clubs for ages 10 to 14). Whether you must be a Scout was not stated. Find a unit through the Council Locator.
how_to_apply: Use the Council Locator on exploring.org or joinexploring.org to find a unit near you.
notes: Exploring.org was only readable in part; fees, Scouting membership rules and California posts were not listed. The page names Learning for Life Corporation in its copyright line. apply_url is the joinexploring.org home page, which has an Enter ZIP Code box for Exploring posts and clubs near you. On exploring.org, the Council Locator heading links to the contact page, and the scouting.org Local Council Locator finds a council, not a unit.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Fees are not stated on the site; ask the post.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12, entered as a team. A faculty advisor registers the team. Each school may enter one team and one submission. Team size and other rules are in the rule book, which the page links to.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to be your team advisor. The advisor signs up the team online. The advisor also emails a form from your principal to nyeconed@ny.frb.org. The page covers team entries only.
notes: The Chicago Fed page says teams register through the same national process and lists the same Feb 15, 2027 deadline. Good for a club, econ class or debate team.
duration: Registration Sept 10, 2026 to Feb 15, 2027. Paper due Mar 15, 2027.
pay_detail: No pay. No fee is listed.

who_can_apply: Open access and free. The page does not state an age minimum, so check the terms and the Minors privacy notice.
how_to_apply: Create a free account and pick a simulation at theforage.com.
notes: Good for a resume line, but it is not a job or an internship. The page has no age minimum and links a privacy notice for minors, so read the terms and ask a parent before signing up.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Aimed at girls and young women in tech. The page does not spell out the rule for other genders, so ask. Clubs meet 1 to 2 hours a week; Pathways is virtual and self-paced.
how_to_apply: Use Get Started on girlswhocode.com/programs to find a Club or begin Pathways.
notes: The page lists no cohort dates. A separate program for ages 18 to 25 also exists.
duration: 1 to 2 hours per week for Clubs
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Free forever for teenagers.
how_to_apply: Join through hackclub.com and find or start a club.
notes: Free for teens. The page lists about 1,500 clubs and events such as game jams and a hardware hackathon in San Francisco.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Open to everyone. The page does not state an age limit. In 2026, pull requests no longer count toward rewards.
how_to_apply: Sign in on hacktoberfest.com with MyMLH, or register for a local fest.
notes: The page states no age limit; check each local fest for age rules. Pull requests no longer count toward rewards in 2026. Earn three stickers to get a sticker pack by mail, and you must sign in with MyMLH and give an address.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register for classes through the link on the program page.
notes: Classes and grades appear on your college transcript and can transfer to other colleges. The web address says hpu-500 but the page is titled HPU 600 and lists $600.
pay_detail: $600 per class

who_can_apply: Students in health science or biomedical science programs, or interested in health careers. Join through a school chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your health science teacher for the chapter advisor.
notes: HOSA reports over 200,000 members in 51 chartered associations. California chapter rules, dues and middle school eligibility were not on the page.
pay_detail: Dues were not stated on the page. Ask your advisor.

who_can_apply: Any high school student who wants to serve and lead. Clubs are set up in high schools or equivalent schools. Members are expected to do at least 50 hours of service a year.
how_to_apply: Use the Find a Key Club tool on keyclub.org, or follow the Start a Key Club steps if your school has none.
notes: Dues and local rules vary by club; dues amount not stated on the pages. Key Club International phone: 800-549-2647.
pay_detail: No pay. Members pay nominal dues (amount not listed on the program pages).

who_can_apply: Open to anyone. The site says its mission is a free education for anyone, anywhere. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Go to the page, pick a course, and sign up for a free account if you want to save progress.
notes: The page loads slowly because it builds in your browser. Course list seen: Financial Literacy, Personal Finance, Entrepreneurship, Careers, College admissions, Career Exploration.
pay_detail: Free (the site says it is a nonprofit offering free education)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18; no prior experience required for the free onboarding programs. Camps run in several cities including San Francisco and Oakland, plus virtual.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form linked on the Kode With Klossy programs page.
notes: Free for all programs. Workforce development programs are for ages 18 to 26, not high schoolers. Camp dates and sites for summer 2027 are not posted yet.
duration: Code-a-Bration is 2 days; Camp is 2 weeks
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students finishing grades 9 to 12 from Wisconsin, across the U.S. and abroad. Admission usually looks at advanced coursework, a 3.2 unweighted GPA or similar, and essays. No age range is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application with two essays (about 500 words total) and an unofficial transcript.
notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.
pay_detail: 2026: domestic residential $4,750; commuter $2,850; international $5,100; plus a $100 application fee (fee waivers can be requested). Scholarships exist (see notes).

who_can_apply: Students finishing grades 9 to 12. Admission usually looks at a 3.0 unweighted GPA or similar, coursework, interest in the course and essays. No age range is stated. The page lists tuition for domestic and international students and says students connect with peers from across the country.
how_to_apply: Online application with two short essays (about 500 words total) and an unofficial transcript. Decisions come on the 2nd and 4th Monday of each month.
notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited and first come, first served. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.
pay_detail: 2026: domestic residential $4,450; commuter $2,600; international $4,800; plus a $100 application fee (fee waivers can be requested). Scholarships exist (see notes).

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Need at least a year each of algebra and geometry, a 3.0 unweighted GPA and a strong interest in math, science and engineering. Highly selective.
how_to_apply: Online application, a high school transcript and a recommendation form. Questions: esp@engr.wisc.edu.
notes: Students live in Dejope Hall with supervision from staff and undergraduate counselors. Laundry and vending cost extra.
pay_detail: Free: housing and meals included. No stipend is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Domestic and international high school students with a high-intermediate (B2 or higher) level of English.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Now link on the course page.
notes: After the first four weeks the course meets once a week. Two optional office hours with instructors.
duration: January 18 to April 1, 2027. Live Mondays and Thursdays 7:00 to 8:30 pm CST and Saturdays 9:00 to 10:30 am CST
pay_detail: Per student: $450 individual, $375 in a two-person team, $325 in a team of three or four.

who_can_apply: Rules differ by event. On the 2027 events list only one event (hackPHS in New Jersey) is marked High School. The Fellowship page gives no age or student rule. Read each event page.
how_to_apply: Browse the events list on mlh.com and read each event's age rule before registering.
notes: The pages did not state a minimum age. Many MLH events are aimed at college students, so check before you plan travel.
pay_detail: Event costs are not listed on the program pages; check each event. The Fellowship pays a stipend (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or older when they apply, in 10th to 12th grade, with at least a 3.2 GPA.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. Add your official high school transcript and one recommendation from a teacher or counselor. List your top three course choices. Test scores are optional.
notes: Costs money. The page also calls the group rising juniors and seniors in places. Confirm your grade with the Summer Academy (academicsuccess@morehouse.edu). Dates shown are from the 2026 summer. The page says the program serves students from across the metro Atlanta area and beyond, and that courses are offered online.
duration: About 6 weeks (June 1 to July 10 in 2026, finals July 6 to 10)
pay_detail: $3,500 flat fee for up to three courses, plus up to $100 per course for books and a $30 non-refundable application fee

who_can_apply: Open to everyone, and no citizenship is needed. Age rules vary by project: some (GLOBE Observer, NeMO-Net) are marked kid friendly; Growing Beyond Earth is for middle and high school teachers.
how_to_apply: Browse the project list, pick one, and follow that project's own sign-up steps.
notes: Some projects need a telescope or other gear. Projects are free to join.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents attending a U.S.-based high school; rising juniors, seniors, or college freshmen; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; at least one high school biology course; a computer with stable internet.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a PDF high school transcript when the window opens.
notes: The real NASA Ames option for high schoolers. NASA's main OSTEM internships are college-only. Acceptance was rolling through April 30, 2026, and the cap was 1,000 applications, so apply early. Needs a PDF high school transcript. No 2027 dates posted.
pay_detail: Free. No stipends since 2026.

who_can_apply: High school students. David Ricardo is for first-timers with no more than one economics course. Team size and school rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form on the challenge page (choose Teacher, Parent, Student or Friend) to get a message when registration opens. Phone: 212-827-3600.
notes: Few details are posted yet. Ask an economics teacher to be your team contact. Confirm first.
pay_detail: No pay. Cash prizes. Cost to enter is not stated.

who_can_apply: Mostly low-income 16 to 24 year olds. You must be a U.S. citizen, a legal resident or allowed to work in the U.S. If you are under 18, a parent, guardian or approved adult must agree and meet an admissions rep. Some rules apply about drug use and criminal history.
how_to_apply: Make an account on the sign-up site. Fill out the application. Interview with an admissions rep. Send papers such as your ID and proof that you are a citizen or resident. A campus review can take up to 30 days.
notes: The FAQ says you may get in faster if you are homeless. It does not name foster youth, so ask an admissions rep. Only enter your ID or Social Security number on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. Check that your nearest campus is open before you plan around it.
duration: Between 8 months and 3 years, depending on the training
pay_detail: Free for students. A living allowance is paid every two weeks and goes up as training moves along. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 who are out of school and out of work. YouthBuild mainly serves people without a high school diploma and with little money. Local sites set their own rules.
how_to_apply: Use the program map on the YouthBuild site to find a program near you, then contact it.
notes: The site says more than 300 programs run in seven countries. The program pages do not confirm a site in Elgin, Chicago, Atlanta, New York or Los Angeles. Use the map.
pay_detail: Not stated on the national page. Ask the local program.

who_can_apply: High school students who can show they know English. The page says students 12 and younger are not allowed. Students who have already graduated are not allowed either.
how_to_apply: Sign up online. Use the Register Now button on the Global Training Initiative page (event ID OGE-F26-GC). When you sign up, you get access to the Knowledge Database.
notes: Deadline is very close. Run by NC State, but open to students anywhere.
duration: One weekend, online (Saturday 8am to Sunday 8pm Eastern)
pay_detail: $299. $30 off before Sept 27. $50 off for past GTI participants.

who_can_apply: You must be in high school now, in grade 10 or higher. International students need English test scores.
how_to_apply: Apply on the GTI website.
notes: Dates are last year's.
pay_detail: $1,295. Early registration discounts and partial scholarships (short essay).

who_can_apply: The Impact League is for ages 13 to 24. Younger kids (5 to 12) enter the Imagination League. Single entries and teams are both allowed.
how_to_apply: Go to innovation.nfte.com and submit your entry before the deadline. The announcement page does not give step-by-step rules, so read the full rules on that site.
notes: Online, so it works from any city. The Impact League age range runs past 18, so you compete with college-age entrants too (page does not say whether groups are judged separately). NFTE also holds a Youth Entrepreneurship Showcase in New York City on Nov 18 to 19, 2026; the page did not say who can attend.
duration: Entries due Dec 13, 2026. Winners announced in spring 2027.
pay_detail: Free to enter. Cash prizes of $300 to $1,500 for winning entries.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, permanent US residents, and able to commute daily. Nearly all sites are day programs with no housing.
how_to_apply: Check the NPS YCC page in late January or early February 2027 for the park list and contacts, then apply to the park you want.
notes: Applications are closed right now. Each park runs its own program, so check whether a park near you takes part. Contact the national office through the link on the NPS page with general questions.
duration: 8 to 10 weeks (can go up to 18), usually 40 hours per week
pay_detail: At least the higher of the state or federal minimum wage, usually for a 40 hour week

who_can_apply: Any high school student interested in any major. Go to one session or all of them.
how_to_apply: Use the register link for each session on the Business Bootcamp page. Sessions run on Zoom.
notes: The page did not print the year next to the session dates, so check the dates when you sign up. A search summary named a separate High School Business Academy in Manhattan. Its page was not read and its cost is unknown.
duration: One hour per session, 7 to 8 pm
pay_detail: Free. You get a certificate of completion for each session you attend.

who_can_apply: In-person group: high school students in the Greater Pittsburgh area. Virtual group: high school students beyond the Greater Pittsburgh Area. The page lists no ages or grades beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the in-person or the virtual application form on the page. Questions: Taylor Goodman, development coordinator, tgoodman@greaterpawv.wish.org.
notes: In-person meetings are at the Make-A-Wish office, Koppers Building, 436 7th Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15219.
duration: In-person: usually the first Tuesday of each month, 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. Virtual: about every other month, usually a third Tuesday.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No pay stated.

who_can_apply: Red Cross says the in-person Babysitter's Training is for ages 11 to 16, and its online Babysitting Basics course is designed for youth 11 and older.
how_to_apply: Pick a class on the Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care page, or buy the online course there.
notes: The old take-a-class/babysitting-training link no longer works, so the page address was updated. Red Cross says these courses do not qualify you for state-licensed child care. Casual babysitting in a private home does not need a work permit per the California child labor guide (2013 edition).
duration: Online course: about 4 hours; in-person length varies
pay_detail: Babysitting Basics Online costs $45 (4 hours, self-paced, certificate valid 2 years). In-person class prices vary by location.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 or equivalent. You cannot enter ISEF directly; you must win at a Society-affiliated fair. Use the Find-a-Fair tool for California fairs.
how_to_apply: Use Find-a-Fair on the Society for Science site, then register with your school or regional fair.
notes: Projects can include no more than 12 months of continuous research. The 2027 ISEF is in California, which can lower travel costs for California finalists. The ISEF site says students from nearly every state in the U.S. and more than 60 countries, regions, and territories compete at affiliated fairs.
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the program pages; more than $7 million in awards and prizes

who_can_apply: Students in their last year of high school who live and attend school in the US or its territories, any citizenship. You need your own original research with real data, plus essays, a paper of up to 20 pages, recommendations and a transcript.
how_to_apply: Apply online at the Society for Science application portal (sciencetalentsearch.smapply.org).
notes: Seniors only, so juniors should plan for next fall. Test scores are optional. Homeschooled students may apply.
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the program pages; $3.1 million in annual awards, $250,000 first place

who_can_apply: Students about to start their last year of high school (juniors). Seniors are not eligible. Open to US citizens, permanent residents and students from participating countries. Needs essays, recommendations, a transcript and test scores.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CEE site. You need essays, two or three teacher letters, an official transcript, and PSAT, SAT, ACT or AP scores.
notes: Very hard to get in. The CEE FAQ says it accepts less than 2.5% of applicants. It is held at MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts, so plan for travel. The program page says RSI 2027 also runs at Stanford for 50 scholars. Check which site applies to you. The FAQ says the program lasts six weeks. It says you must be 16 by July 1 of the program year. It lists a $75 application fee that is not refundable, with waivers for need. The program page says the program is free to students. Ask CEE which is right.
duration: Six weeks (one week of classes, five weeks of research)
pay_detail: Free to students

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0. Online courses require age 14 by the course start date. Entry is by application. The intro course (BE-BOAT) comes first.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You hear back 7 to 10 business days later. Payment is due within 2 weeks of acceptance.
notes: Costs a lot. The program page says it cannot offer financial aid, grants or scholarships to participants at this time. Email precollege@ucsd.edu with questions. The page has a section for international students in the last call, with extra shipping fees for loaner lab kits.
duration: About 7 weeks (Winter 2027 BioImaging and 3D-Printing course: Jan 9 to Feb 27, 2027)
pay_detail: Tuition $2,700 for the BE-BOAT intro course. Other course prices are on the course pages.

who_can_apply: Middle school, high school and college students in career and technical education, in a school chapter. Virtual chapters exist for students without a classroom chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your CTE teacher, or use the 12 Steps to Start a Chapter or Virtual Chapter on skillsusa.org. Phone 844-875-4557, email customercare@skillsusa.org.
notes: Most useful if your school has a trades or tech CTE pathway.
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the program pages; ask your CTE teacher.

who_can_apply: Currently in grades 8 to 11 and older than 13 and younger than 19 during the program dates. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with unofficial transcripts and the application fee; rank up to three courses. Financial aid is a separate form due about a week after the deadline.
notes: Pay-to-play. Prices and dates are from 2026. The page says to join the mailing list for future dates. Admissions page (checked 2026-10-10) says 'older than 13 and younger than 19 during the program dates'. The tuition page gives the $60 fee for financial aid applications; the admissions page gives $65.
duration: Two weeks, live online (2026: June 15 to 26 or July 6 to 17)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition $3,200. Application fee $65 (the aid page says $60); waivers on request. Limited need-based aid. Some courses need materials costing up to $100.

who_can_apply: The page says it is designed for grades 4 to 12, college learners and adults. It mentions guides for after-school and homeschool groups. It does not say whether a student can sign up with no teacher or group.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Register Now button. The registration wizard shows the program rules and key dates. Ask a teacher, club leader or parent whether your school or group already signs up.
notes: The page does not say whether a student can register alone; it talks about teams and group guides. Price was not stated beyond 'no cost or low cost'. Confirm first.
duration: Several weeks to a full school year, your choice
pay_detail: No pay. The page says it is available at no cost or low cost.

who_can_apply: High school students looking to get ahead or recover credit. The site mentions free options for California public schools and scholarship applications for eligible students.
how_to_apply: Enroll from the courses page, ask your school counselor about school-paid seats, or call (408) 450-4962.
notes: This is coursework, not a job. Included because many teens use it to free up schedule time for jobs and internships.
pay_detail: Fees vary by course and prices are not on the home page. The site lists free options for California public schools and scholarships. The page does not say anyone is paid.

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores or juniors who are 16 by July 5 of the program year, interested in STEM, and U.S. citizens. Past SEES interns cannot repeat.
how_to_apply: Apply online at spacegrant.net/apps/sees: essays (maximum 250 words per response), a short intro video (submit the link), an unofficial transcript or report card, and a recommendation form. Travel scholarships are available and do not affect your selection.
notes: Very competitive: about 2,000 applications and 215 accepted in 2024 (FAQ). It is an educational internship, not a paid job.
duration: Online work in June and July plus a 2-week on-site session in Austin (July 5-18 in 2026)
pay_detail: No stipend. Free for scholarship recipients and for virtual participation; paid participants pay $2,000 tuition (meals, housing, tours and local travel included, travel to Austin not included). Travel scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors with a strong interest in engineering, science or math who live in the United States. About 50 students per session are chosen by holistic review. Students from low-income backgrounds or with limited STEM access are strongly encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the MITE page. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: Selective. The page does not list a financial-aid policy; ask cseoutreach@utexas.edu if the $200 is a barrier.
pay_detail: $200, paid only after acceptance (students stay in a campus residence hall)

who_can_apply: Students at partner schools. Schools join by filling out an interest form and talking with a VEI Regional Director.
how_to_apply: Ask your school or counselor about the program. Contact info@veinternational.org or 855-740-6555.
notes: Not an individual sign-up; your school must be a partner. Cost to schools is not posted.
pay_detail: School/district pays (cost not public)

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 on a team of four to six with a teacher advisor.
how_to_apply: A teacher advisor and the team register on the Wharton Global Youth site. The page does not give a date for the next cycle's registration; check the site.
notes: Sign-up steps are on the Rules and Roles and Register pages, which were not read. Travel costs to the finale were not stated.
duration: Trading starts Sept 28, 2026, then virtual semifinals (date not posted) and a finale Apr 29 to 30, 2027 (2026-27 cycle)
pay_detail: Free to enter. No pay.

who_can_apply: Open to almost anyone, even without logging in. The page links to guidance for younger editors but states no minimum age.
how_to_apply: Start editing, or make a free account (not required). Try The Wikipedia Adventure tutorial.
notes: Protect your personal info; do not share your school or address.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident with a valid Social Security number. Teens are picked randomly from across the country, so you do not have to live in Wyoming.
how_to_apply: Apply through the YCC page on the Yellowstone park website when the window opens. Selection is random. Questions: phone 307-344-7381.
notes: Wage and dates above are from the 2026 page. Teen enrollees are randomly selected from across the country.
duration: 1 month (2026 sessions: June 14 to July 15 and July 19 to August 18)
pay_detail: $10.50 an hour for 40 hours a week, with a small food charge (about $3 a day).

who_can_apply: Open to volunteers online. The pages state no age rule; check the user agreement.
how_to_apply: Go to zooniverse.org, pick a project, and make an account if the project asks.
notes: The home page and FAQ do not state a minimum age. Projects span arts, biology, climate, history, language, medicine, nature, physics, space and social science.
pay_detail: No cost stated on the program pages; it is a volunteer research site
